shots.narration: Today is the 24th of December. Christmas Eve.
shots.onScreen: Snowy village at night, warm windows; a snowdrift wobbles and Flurry the snowman pushes up out of it, shakes off snow and blinks awake
shots.motion: slow push in on the snowdrift
shots.sfx: soft wind, sleigh bells, snow puff

shots.narration: Well, it is on the day this video goes up. If you are watching later, hello, future person! Tell us in the comments what happened.
shots.onScreen: Flurry hops toward camera and waves with a twig arm; a speech-bubble comment floats up beside him

shots.narration: Tomorrow, the whole world celebrates Christmas. Even in countries where most people are not Christian.
shots.onScreen: A night globe slowly turning in space, warm lights twinkle on across it one by one

shots.narration: Japan is a great example. Very few Christians, but trees, lights, gifts and parties everywhere.
shots.onScreen: Flurry slides along a lantern-lit street with a giant lit tree, paper lanterns sway

shots.narration: But here is the twist. Jesus was probably not born on the 25th of December.
shots.onScreen: Flurry holds up a big calendar page DEC 25; it flips over to a giant question mark; Flurry's eyes go wide

shots.narration: And the tree, the mistletoe, the carols, the feast? Most of them are older than Christmas itself.
shots.onScreen: Tree, mistletoe, songbook and roast slide in around Flurry one by one; his carrot nose droops in shock

shots.narration: So grab a hot chocolate. Let's find out where Christmas really comes from.
shots.onScreen: Flurry jumps on a red sled and zooms down a snowy hill past pine trees, hot chocolate steaming
shots.motion: fast tracking shot beside the sled

shots.narration: Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ, the central figure of Christianity.
shots.onScreen: Night over Bethlehem, flat-roofed stone houses, palms, one huge bright star

shots.narration: Christians believe he is the son of God. And almost all historians agree he was a real person, who lived about two thousand years ago.
shots.onScreen: An old book opens on a reading stand by lamplight; Flurry peeks over it, nodding

shots.narration: The Gospels of Luke and Matthew tell the story. Joseph and Mary travel from Nazareth to Bethlehem, for a census.
shots.onScreen: Joseph walks leading a grey donkey carrying Mary along a desert road at dusk; Flurry hops along behind in a tiny headscarf
shots.overlay: callout: NAZARETH TO BETHLEHEM / FOR A ROMAN CENSUS

shots.narration: There is no room to stay. So the baby is born in a stable, and laid in a manger.
shots.onScreen: Warm lantern-lit stable, straw, ox and donkey, Mary and Joseph kneel by the manger

shots.narration: Angels announce a saviour. Shepherds come to see him, and wise men follow a star.
shots.onScreen: Hillside with shepherds and sheep looking up at a glowing light; three wise men on camels follow the star across the dunes

shots.narration: A beautiful story. With one small problem. It never says the date.
shots.onScreen: Flurry flips frantically through a giant book, then shrugs with both twig arms

shots.narration: Around the year 200, a scholar called Clement of Alexandria wrote that some people had worked out the exact day.
shots.onScreen: A scholar writes at a desk piled with scrolls in a sunlit library with columns
shots.overlay: callout: CLEMENT OF ALEXANDRIA / SCHOLAR, EGYPT

shots.narration: Their answer? The 25th of the Egyptian month of Pachon. That is around the 20th of May.
shots.onScreen: A big calendar flips from PACHON 25 to MAY 20; Flurry pops on sunglasses

shots.narration: May! So how did we end up in the middle of winter?
shots.onScreen: Snow starts falling on Flurry in his sunglasses; he shivers and tugs his scarf tight

shots.narration: The first recorded Christmas was in Rome, on the 25th of December, in the year 336.
shots.onScreen: Roman temple courtyard at winter morning, people in togas, banners, braziers

shots.narration: And that date was already a party. It sat right by the winter solstice, the darkest time of the year, when Romans honoured their sun god, Sol Invictus, the Unconquered Sun.
shots.onScreen: A golden statue with a ray crown on a plinth; the sun rises behind the temple and light sweeps across the crowd
shots.motion: push in as the sun rises
shots.overlay: callout: SOL INVICTUS / THE UNCONQUERED SUN

shots.narration: Christians already linked Jesus with light. One Bible verse even says, unto you shall the sun of righteousness arise.
shots.onScreen: A scroll unrolls and its lines glow gold; rays spread from it

shots.narration: So as Christianity grew in the Roman Empire, the church picked the solstice for the birth of Christ. One historian calls it cosmic symbolism. The day the sun is reborn.
shots.onScreen: Sun breaks over a snowy horizon; Flurry squints, starts to sweat a little and fans himself with his hat

shots.narration: Long before Christmas, winter festivals were the biggest parties of the year across Europe.
shots.onScreen: Snowy pine forest clearing at night, a bonfire, villagers in furs dancing in a ring

shots.narration: The Celts brought mistletoe and ivy into their winter celebrations.
shots.onScreen: A druid in a white robe reaches up into an oak to cut mistletoe; Flurry stands under the hanging mistletoe and looks around, embarrassed

shots.narration: The Norse and the Anglo-Saxons celebrated Yule. Yes, that Yule.
shots.onScreen: A long wooden Norse hall in snow with carved dragon gables, smoke from the roof

shots.narration: They feasted on boar and goat, and burned the Yule log, a real tree trunk, chosen and dragged home for the festival.
shots.onScreen: Villagers drag a huge log on ropes across the snow into the hall; inside a fire roars and a feast table waits

shots.narration: In Rome, the solstice festival of Saturnalia had feasting and gift giving too.
shots.onScreen: Romans around a long table hand each other small wrapped gifts, laughing

shots.narration: In Eastern Europe, singers went from house to house for Koleda. That tradition grew into the Christmas carol.
shots.onScreen: Carol singers with a star lantern walk door to door in a snowy village; Flurry joins the end of the line, music notes float up

shots.narration: And the Christmas tree? Its story starts in medieval Livonia, today's Estonia and Latvia, where German merchants put up decorated trees.
shots.onScreen: Medieval town square with timber houses; a tree hung with apples and candles in the middle; merchants admire it
shots.overlay: callout: LIVONIA / TODAY ESTONIA AND LATVIA

shots.narration: Later, German Protestants brought trees into their homes. The Catholic Church resisted for centuries. The Vatican did not get its first Christmas tree until 1982.
shots.onScreen: A huge tree rises in a grand square in front of a domed church; Flurry taps his wrist like checking a watch
shots.motion: low angle push up the tree

shots.narration: Some customs are religious. In 1223, Saint Francis of Assisi popularised the nativity scene, and it spread across Europe.
shots.onScreen: A candle-lit church with a small nativity crib; a friar in a brown robe sets a figure down
shots.overlay: callout: SAINT FRANCIS OF ASSISI / NATIVITY SCENE

shots.narration: Even the colours mean something. Red for the blood of Christ, green for eternal life, gold for the gifts of the wise men.
shots.onScreen: Three giant baubles, red, green and gold, swing down on ribbons and light up one by one

shots.narration: Or, if you ask the shops, red for Santa and green for the tree.
shots.onScreen: Flurry winks, pulls a Santa hat onto his head, a tree slides in beside him

shots.narration: Which brings us to the biggest star of all. Santa Claus.
shots.onScreen: Spotlight snaps on a snowy rooftop chimney; Flurry drumrolls on a bucket

shots.narration: His story begins with a real man, Saint Nicholas, born in the late 200s in what is now Turkey.
shots.onScreen: A sunny Mediterranean town with white houses; a bishop in red robes and a tall mitre walks the street
shots.overlay: callout: SAINT NICHOLAS / MYRA, TODAY'S TURKEY

shots.narration: He was known for kindness. It is said he gave away all his inherited wealth to people in need, and he became the protector of children.
shots.onScreen: At night Nicholas drops a small bag of coins through a window; inside, children wake up and cheer

shots.narration: His feast day falls in December. So, over time, he got tied to Christmas.
shots.onScreen: A calendar page shows 6 DECEMBER, slides along to 25 DECEMBER

shots.narration: Dutch families brought him to America. In 1773, a New York newspaper reported them honouring Sinterklaas. Say Sinterklaas fast, and you get Santa Claus.
shots.onScreen: An old newspaper spins in; the word SINTERKLAAS squeezes and morphs into SANTA CLAUS while Flurry says it faster and faster

shots.narration: In 1841, thousands of children lined up at a Philadelphia shop to see a life-size Santa. After that, Santa was everywhere.
shots.onScreen: An old shop window with a life-size Santa model, a long line of children in coats outside in the snow
shots.sfx: crowd of kids, bell on door

shots.narration: Early Santas often wore green, blue, or white. Coca-Cola's adverts in the 1930s made the jolly red Santa famous all over the world.
shots.onScreen: A Santa figure's coat changes colour green, blue, white, then red; Flurry spins dizzy watching

shots.narration: And why the North Pole? Thank the cartoonist Thomas Nast, drawing for Harper's Weekly from 1863. The reindeer came with the address.
shots.onScreen: Icy North Pole with a striped pole, a reindeer team and a red sleigh; Flurry pats a reindeer

shots.narration: Other countries have their own gift bringers. In Germany and Switzerland, it is the Christkind, an angel-like child.
shots.onScreen: A glowing golden-haired angel child in white floats over a snowy German street with gifts

shots.narration: In Scandinavia, a little elf called the Jultomte rides a sleigh pulled by goats.
shots.onScreen: A small bearded elf in a red cap drives a sleigh pulled by two goats through snowy pines

shots.narration: Finland's Joulupukki, the Yule Goat, started out rather scary, before he became a friendly Santa.
shots.onScreen: A shaggy goat-horned figure in a dark doorway; a puff of snow and he becomes a smiling Santa; Flurry hides, then laughs

shots.narration: And in Italy, La Befana, a kind old witch on a broomstick, slides down the chimney with toys.
shots.onScreen: A witch on a broomstick flies over moonlit rooftops and dives into a chimney

shots.narration: Through the Middle Ages, Christmas came and went. At first, a bigger day was Epiphany, the 6th of January, when the wise men visited.
shots.onScreen: Three wise men on camels crest a dune at sunrise under the star

shots.narration: In Spain, it is still the Day of the Kings, and that is when many children open their presents.
shots.onScreen: Spanish street parade with three kings on a float throwing sweets; children in a living room open gifts

shots.narration: Soon December took over. The twelve days of Christmas began, another echo of Saturnalia.
shots.onScreen: Twelve candles light up one after another along a long table

shots.narration: Kings loved it. Charlemagne was crowned on Christmas Day in the year 800. So was William the Conqueror, in 1066.
shots.onScreen: A stone church throne room; a crown is lowered onto a king's head; a second king in mail follows

shots.narration: And in 1377, King Richard the Second threw a Christmas feast where guests ate 28 oxen and 300 sheep.
shots.onScreen: A huge medieval feast hall, a long table piled with roasts, a tally counting oxen and sheep; Flurry sits at the end looking very full

shots.narration: Back then, gifts often went between landlords and tenants, not just family. And they were swapped on the 6th of January.
shots.onScreen: A lord at a manor door receives a basket from a tenant and hands back a wrapped gift

shots.narration: In the 1500s and 1600s, during the Reformation, many Protestants moved gift giving to the 24th and the 25th.
shots.onScreen: A family by a fire hands out gifts; a calendar slides from 6 JAN to 25 DEC

shots.narration: Some strict Puritans even banned Christmas for a while. It did not last.
shots.onScreen: A stern Puritan nails up a BANNED sign; a snowball from Flurry knocks it off
shots.motion: static wide, then whip to Flurry

shots.narration: In Britain, Christmas Day became a bank holiday in 1834. And German-born Queen Charlotte brought the Christmas tree to the royal court.
shots.onScreen: A Georgian palace parlour; Queen Charlotte in a gown beside a tree lit with candles

shots.narration: And by 1848, a famous picture of the royal family around their tree made one a must-have in every home.
shots.onScreen: A gilded picture frame shows a royal family around a tree; it pulls back to many homes with trees in their windows

shots.narration: Winter has always been a time to celebrate, whatever you believe.
shots.onScreen: A snowy town square at dusk full of people, lights strung between houses

shots.narration: Jewish families celebrate Hanukkah, the eight-night festival of lights. Its dates move with the Hebrew calendar.
shots.onScreen: A menorah in a frosty window; candles light one by one

shots.narration: Muslims celebrate Eid al-Fitr at the end of Ramadan, and it moves through the year. Fun fact: Islam honours Jesus as a prophet.
shots.onScreen: Lanterns and a crescent moon over a family dinner table

shots.narration: Kwanzaa, a celebration of African-American heritage, starts on the 26th of December and lasts seven days.
shots.onScreen: A kinara with seven candles, three red, one black, three green, lights up on a table

shots.narration: And millions of people, of every faith or none, simply enjoy the lights, the food, the gifts and time with family.
shots.onScreen: Flurry and a crowd of villagers gather around a giant lit tree in the square

shots.narration: So that is Christmas. A birthday on a borrowed date. A tree from Livonia. A log from the Norse. Carols from Koleda. And a saint from Turkey in a red suit.
shots.onScreen: The tree, log, carol star and Santa hat orbit Flurry one after another

shots.narration: However you celebrate, tell us in the comments how you spend it. And subscribe for more stories like this.
shots.onScreen: Flurry points at a big glowing subscribe bell that swings in

shots.narration: From all of us, and from Flurry... Happy Christmas!
shots.onScreen: Flurry and the reindeer wave; fireworks burst over the snowy village and HAPPY CHRISTMAS lights up in the sky
